Events in reverse mode

Source: vignettes/articles/methods-reverse-events.Rmd
methods-reverse-events.Rmd

Adjoint of an event to first and second order, with the transpose of the Heun transport Events (2). Notation; arguments events and derivMode = "reverse" or "forward-reverse" of cppODE(), cotangent of solveODE(). Derivatives are in \(\theta = (x_0, p)\); event times \(t_e\) and root functions \(g_e\) depend on \(\theta\) through \(p\).

Adjoint of an event

An event is a separate map between two steps. The Heun transport shifts to the event surface, resets, and shifts back to the grid time, each shift over the firing-time residual \(\delta t^{*}\), zero in value with nonzero derivatives. It reduces to the saltation relation \[ \mathrm{d}x^{+} = R'\!\left(\mathrm{d}x^{-} + f^{-}\, \delta t^{*}\right) - f^{+}\, \delta t^{*}, \tag{1} \] with \(R\) the resets and \(R'\) their Jacobian. For a root event \(g_e(x, t, p) = 0\), \(\delta t^{*} = -(\nabla_x g_e \cdot \mathrm{d}x + \partial g_e/\partial p \cdot \mathrm{d}p) / \dot g_e\) by the implicit function theorem; for a time-triggered event at \(t^{*} = t_e(p)\), \(\delta t^{*} = (\partial t_e/\partial p)\cdot \mathrm{d}p\).

Contracted with the cotangent \(\lambda^{+}\) after the jump, the \(\delta t^{*}\) terms of the linear map (1) collect into one scalar \(\eta\), \[ \eta = \left(\lambda^{+}\right)^{\mathsf T} \left(R' f^{-} - f^{+}\right), \qquad \lambda^{-} = R'^{\mathsf T}\lambda^{+} + \eta \left(\frac{\partial\, \delta t^{*}}{\partial x}\right)^{\!\mathsf T}, \tag{2} \] and the parameter cotangent gains \(\eta\,(\partial\, \delta t^{*}/\partial p)^{\mathsf T}\):

event state gains parameters gain
root \(-(\eta/\dot g_e)\nabla_x g_e\) \(-(\eta/\dot g_e)\,\partial g_e/\partial p\)
time-triggered nothing \(\eta\,\partial t_e/\partial p\)

\(R'^{\mathsf T}\) is applied reset by reset, in reverse order: a replacement removes the component cotangent, an addition keeps it, a multiplication by \(v\) scales it by \(v\), plus the derivatives of a state- or parameter-dependent \(v\). The adjoint of a jump needs \(f\) at both ends, \(\nabla_x g_e\), \(\dot g_e\) and the derivatives of reset and event-time expressions; no Jacobian of \(f\), since every shift term has the residual as a factor.

Multistep methods restart after a jump from \(z_0 = x\), \(z_1 = h\, f(x, t)\), other slots zero, \(h\) the first step size, so the history cotangent \(\bar z_j\) collapses onto \(x\): \[ \bar x = \bar z_0 + h\, J^{\mathsf T} \bar z_1, \qquad \bar p = h \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial p}\right)^{\!\mathsf T} \bar z_1, \tag{3} \] and higher slots nothing, as at the start of the trajectory.

Second order at an event

\(\delta t^{*}\) is zero in value with a nonzero first derivative, so \[ (\delta t^{*})^{2} = 0, \qquad \mathrm{d}(\delta t^{*})^{2} = 2\, \delta t^{*}\,\mathrm{d}\,\delta t^{*} = 0, \qquad \mathrm{d}^{2}(\delta t^{*})^{2} = 2\,(\mathrm{d}\,\delta t^{*})^{2} \neq 0 , \tag{4} \] so terms of order \((\delta t^{*})^{2}\) drop from the gradient but not from the Hessian. Three such terms enter a jump, for time-triggered events (\(\delta t^{*} = t_e - \mathrm{scalar}(t_e)\)) as for root events: both use the same transport, transposed as a reversed program. If the jump height moves with a parameter, (1) alone is exact in value but wrong in the tangents: the backward shift \(\bar x^{*}_{+} = \bigl(I - \delta t^{*}\, J(x^{*}_{+})\bigr)^{\mathsf T}\bar x^{+}\) multiplies \(\delta t^{*}\) by a factor nonzero in value.

Curvature of the shift. Each half of the transport is a Heun step, \[ x^{*} = x^{-} + f^{-}\, \delta t^{*} + \tfrac{1}{2}\, \kappa^{-}\, (\delta t^{*})^{2}, \qquad \kappa = \frac{\partial f}{\partial x} f + \frac{\partial f}{\partial t}, \tag{5} \] with \(\kappa\,\delta t^{*}\) the difference of the two right-hand sides the step evaluates, so no Jacobian.

Post-jump state. The checkpoint keeps only \(x^{-}\). A reconstruction of \(x^{+}\) by the bare reset would give \(\partial x^{+} / \partial t^{*} = 0\), whereas \[ \frac{\partial x^{+}}{\partial t^{*}} = f^{-} - f^{+} , \tag{6} \] so the reconstruction runs the transport, not the reset.

Quadrature. The parameter cotangent \[ \bar p_{k} = \int_{t_0}^{T} q_{k}\,\mathrm{d}t = \int_{t_0}^{t^{*}} q_{k}\,\mathrm{d}t + \int_{t^{*}}^{T} q_{k}\,\mathrm{d}t, \qquad q_{k} = \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial p_{k}}\right)^{\!\mathsf T}\!\lambda, \tag{7} \] is split at \(t^{*}\), where \(q_{k}\) jumps; the moving split point contributes \[ \frac{\partial \bar p_{k}}{\partial \theta} \;\supset\; \Big( q_{k}(t^{*-}) - q_{k}(t^{*+}) \Big)\, \frac{\partial t^{*}}{\partial \theta} . \tag{8} \] Only parameters whose \(\partial f / \partial p_{k}\) depends on a reset state contribute.

All three are scaled by the residual, zero in value with tangent \(\partial t^{*} / \partial \theta\), and leave the gradient unchanged. The root-event residual is \[ \delta t^{*} = -\,\frac{g_e - \mathrm{scalar}(g_e)}{\dot g_e}, \qquad \dot g_e = \frac{\partial g_e}{\partial t} + \nabla_x g_e \cdot f , \tag{9} \] read at the checkpointed state, which holds \(\partial x / \partial \theta\) at a fixed time since localization ignores tangents; \(\nabla_x g_e\) contracts it to the firing time.

Transpose of the root transport

With the names of Events (2), the jump is the composition \[ \begin{aligned} x_{E} &= x^{-} + f_{1}\, \delta t^{*}, & x^{*} &= x^{-} + \tfrac{1}{2}(f_{1} + f_{2})\, \delta t^{*}, & x^{*}_{+} &= R(x^{*}, t^{*}), \\ x_{B} &= x^{*}_{+} - \tilde f_{1}\, \delta t^{*}, & x^{+} &= x^{*}_{+} - \tfrac{1}{2}(\tilde f_{1} + \tilde f_{2})\, \delta t^{*}, & \end{aligned} \tag{10} \] with \(f_{2} = f(x_{E}, t^{*})\), \(\tilde f_{1} = f(x^{*}_{+}, t^{*})\) and \(f_{1}\), \(\tilde f_{2}\) at the grid time \(t_*^{(0)}\). The program is transposed assignment by assignment. A closed form pruned by order in \(\delta t^{*}\) is valid for the gradient but, by (4), not for the Hessian.

Every assignment containing the residual contributes to it, two through the \(\theta\)-dependent \(t^{*}\) in \(f_{2}\) and \(\tilde f_{1}\): \[ \overline{\delta t^{*}} \;\supset\; \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}\right)_{\!(x^{*}_{+}, t^{*})}\!\!\cdot \bar{\tilde f}_{1} + \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial t}\right)_{\!(x_{E}, t^{*})}\!\!\cdot \bar f_{2} . \tag{11} \] Both cotangents have a factor \(\delta t^{*}\): (11) is absent from the gradient, at full strength in the Hessian, zero for autonomous \(f\), and missing from a pruned form.

The forward correction \(-\tfrac{1}{2}(\ddot g_e / \dot g_e)\,(\delta t^{*})^{2}\) of the residual, Events (6), has the chain factor \(1 + 2 c_{2}\, \delta t^{*}\), \(c_{2} = -\ddot g_e / (2\dot g_e)\), one in value with a second-order tangent; the transpose applies it to \(\partial\, \delta t^{*} / \partial x\).

The sweep binds the tangent storage of every buffer it passes to a generated contraction (forward over reverse). Jump-transpose reads of such a buffer are multiplied by \(\delta t^{*}\), so an unbound buffer leaves value and gradient correct and the Hessian wrong by a rank-one term.

Derivative of the residual. Since \(\dot g_e\) depends on the state, \[ \frac{\partial\, \delta t^{*}}{\partial x} = -\frac{\nabla_x g_e}{\dot g_e} - \frac{\delta t^{*}}{\dot g_e}\, \nabla_x \dot g_e , \qquad \nabla_x \dot g_e = \nabla_x \frac{\partial g_e}{\partial t} + \left(\nabla_x^{2} g_e\right) f + J^{\mathsf T}\nabla_x g_e , \tag{12} \] with the second term absent from the gradient and at full strength in the Hessian. The generator differentiates \(\dot g_e\) as one expression, so all three terms of \(\nabla_x \dot g_e\) are present, also those vanishing for a time-independent \(g_e\) linear in the state; in \(\theta\) it gives \(\partial^{2} g_e/\partial\theta\,\partial t\), \((\partial \nabla_x g_e/\partial\theta)\cdot f\) and \((\partial f/\partial\theta)^{\mathsf T}\nabla_x g_e\). A forcing in \(g_e\) is differentiated in \(t\) through a rate leaf on the expression graph, printed as the derivative of the PCHIP interpolant.

Time-dependent resets. A reset value \(v\) with explicit time dependence is applied at \(t^{*}\): \[ \frac{\partial x^{*}_{+}}{\partial t^{*}} \;\supset\; c\, \frac{\partial v}{\partial t}, \qquad c = \begin{cases} 1 & \text{add,} \\ 1 & \text{replace,} \\ x^{*}_{k} & \text{multiply,}\end{cases} \tag{13} \] with \(k\) the reset component, a first-order contribution to \(\eta\) of (2): without it the gradient is wrong. The transposed reset therefore receives \(t^{*}\) as a dual, so \(\partial v/\partial\theta\) includes \(\partial t^{*}/\partial\theta\). Such a value evaluates \(t^{*}\) directly and is accurate to the root tolerance, not the integration tolerance; for a value depending only on the state at \(t^{*}\), the smooth trajectory damps the localization error.

With \(R = \mathrm{id}\), (10) is the identity and the transpose cancels term by term. Tests compare the transpose with a nested-dual evaluation of the transport, and the second order over a trajectory with forward over forward on the same steps.

Moving event rows

If \(t^{*}\) depends on a parameter, the row at the firing time moves with it. A functional \(w^{\mathsf T} x\) seeded on that row compares states at different times for different parameters and has no derivative; a cotangent on the requested output times is well posed.
